text.tspan: Phase 1 · Repair-job card and core components · 04 November 2026
For review before extending the system to other screens.
Preserve the approved repair card: navy header, pale canvas, white bordered accordions, compact controls and four-stage repair workflow.
Source audit; named tokens and Inter styles; button, field, status, selection, accordion, feedback and save variants; conditional IW/OOW/WEEE patterns; status icons; a fully editable repair-
Active/archive lists, registration, Returns, shipment details, Spare parts and full add/edit/select modal templates. Do not extend unapproved refinements to these screens yet.
Approved repair-job-full.jpg; repository workspace.css, job-detail.html, repair-workspace.js and workspace-progress.js; established user decisions. No code or production changes are
Priority is consistency, not a new visual direction. Changes below are proposals unless already agreed in the brief.
Inconsistent label gaps and section-specific overrides make controls appear misaligned. Standardise label → control to 6 px, vertical field gap to 14–18 px and column gap to 24 px. Keep
The reference shows a collapsed change-reason chevron while its textarea is visible. Document one disclosure state: hide the body when collapsed; reveal the existing reason field when
expanded. Done sections auto-collapse on entry only.
Existing fetch actions look alike and the external-form button is after its resulting number. Use source-colour fetch actions; put the form-fill action before the SO field in one subtle dashed
A twelve-column table is vulnerable to long serials, labels and status values. Keep all columns, fixed widths, short Docs label, icon selection/delete, 10-character description preview and
keyboard-accessible expansion. Never shrink the entire table to unreadable text.
Explain why an action is unavailable next to it. Loading, validation and retry need text, not only colour. Preserve existing input on failure. Saved/Unsaved/Saving controls occupy a
Keep Delete repair below the histories with a divider and generous separation. The explicit destructive label and confirmation matter more than a large red surface.
Light interface only. No unsolicited dark mode or new brand direction. Variables have explicit scopes and WEB code syntax.
Inter: page title 21/28 Bold; section 17/24 Bold; subheading 15/22 Semi Bold; values/body 13/20 Regular; labels 12/18 Medium; actions 12/18 Semi Bold; support 11/16. Courier remains the
agreed printed-form typeface. Courier is unavailable in this Figma runtime; no inaccurate printed-form specimen is substituted.
Control38 · textarea64 minimum · accordion header60 · number30 · interface icon16–20 · repair status icon24 · card radius5 · control radius4 · modal radius6 · page gutter32 · card body22
· field columns24 · label gap6. Table body13, headers11; do not reduce values to fit.
Cards are flat with a 1 px border and no shadow. Modals/tooltips may use restrained elevation: 0 8 24 rgba(20,38,62,0.14). Focus uses a 2 px blue outline with 2 px offset.
Purpose, anatomy, dimensions, state variants and keyboard rules are also stored on reusable main-component descriptions.
Label + optional 16px leading icon. 38px height, radius4, horizontal padding14. Primary, Secondary and Destructive each have Default/Hover/Focus/Disabled/Loading. Enter/Space
activates. Labels describe actions, not vague confirmation. Icon-only buttons require accessible names and tooltips.
Visible label + 6px gap + control + optional helper/error. Text/Date/Select/Textarea expose editable Label and Value. Default/Hover/Focus/Disabled/Read only/Error. Use native keyboard
date/select behaviour in RB. Required and error states use words as well as colour.
Checkboxes use Space and clear focus. Only eligible free parts are selectable; confirmed order composition stays locked. Inline editors are keyboard reachable. Long descriptions show at
most ten characters including the ellipsis; hover/focus reveals full text.
Header anatomy: chevron, section number, title, completeness badge, summary. Enter/Space toggles; expose aria-expanded. Done/In progress/Pending/Not started describe
completeness, not outcome. Progress counts Done sections only.
Saved disables Save/Discard; Unsaved enables them; Saving prevents duplicate submission. A failure keeps edits and explains retry. If further edits occur during saving, they remain
Modal heading and actions stay visible while the body can scroll. Trap focus; Escape/Cancel closes and restores focus to opener. No destructive confirmation on outside click. Tooltip
supports keyboard focus and Escape, and must not be clipped by table overflow.
Source badges indicate available fetch capability. They are not evidence that a stored value originated in that service.
Targets: model derived from model code, model code, version, purchase date, warranty expiry. Use purchase date when present; otherwise suggest production date and warn. Warranty
uses L. Preview Current/From GSPN/Status before Apply to form; replacing existing data requires a reason. Save stores and audits.
Requires a non-empty original Simpro job. Job site = Site Custom → Store Name/ID; if empty use Site name. Fz = Customer. Received = date of the latest Work Note. Repair comments =
Summary of Works Completed only. The Simpro job field is a manual lookup key, not a fetched target.
Parts fetch requires a saved GSPN SO; it affects the parts table only. Claim fetch is a separate action affecting claim number and amount only. Automatic claim lookup remains
unimplemented and disabled with an explanation. IW claim is a borderless footer shown for IW repairs only.
Fill GSPN service order form comes before the SO field within one dashed border. Available only while SO is empty. It prepares an external form for review; it does not automatically Save.
Visual states reflect existing records; users must not choose an arbitrary icon to make the workflow progress.
OOW shows Copy OOW details plus approver and approval date. Missing OOW approval outlines downstream blocks red; expired warranty outlines Unit details. WEEE requires approver,
approval date and information source, then explicit outcome confirmation.
Create PO applies to free selected parts. Add to draft PO is disabled when no draft exists and offers draft selection when several exist. GSPN confirmation locks order composition.
Remove only free/unordered parts. Bulletins remain linked by part number.
Repaired, QC pass and WEEE require confirmation. Confirmation locks the repair; engineer/date are retained. Archive after seven days, preserving green Repaired, blue QC pass and red
WEEE. A later repair is a new card and shows prior repair history.
DOA received is primary until a replacement draft PO exists. The user may order the replacement before shipping DOA. Outstanding DOA return remains a secondary warning until
dispatched. Do not block replacement ordering on return shipment.
Target is a 1920×1200 physical laptop at Windows150%, browser100%: approximately1280 CSS px wide, with less height after browser chrome.
Approval frame width1280; page gutters32; content1216; inner card1172. All twelve table columns fit within1172. Vertical scrolling is acceptable for the fully expanded reference.
Progressive disclosure reduces routine page height; do not hide required fields or reduce body text to avoid every scroll.
Mobile prioritises reading repair status and details. Complex editing and browser-bridge actions remain desktop-first. Full mobile operations are not part of phase1. Narrow layouts may use
cards or deliberate secondary disclosure rather than shrinking the desktop table.
These are explicit limits, not completed functionality.
Confirm source tags and hover targeting; the 1280px table populated-state readability; icon distinctions at24px; compact button grouping. The attached source contains no IW claim, OOW
or WEEE data; their components are conditional specimens, not changes to that source record.
Courier is not installed in the Figma runtime. This draft supplies visual state variants and behaviour documentation; it is not a fully wired interactive application or tested browser
implementation. Code Connect is not configured in the Thymeleaf repository. Remaining screen templates wait for approval.
Source has hardcoded colours and dimensions rather than reusable CSS tokens. Proposed --rb-* code syntax on Figma variables documents the implementation contract; no claim is
made that those CSS variables already exist. Adopt them in a separate implementation task after approval.
Review order: Foundations & audit → Core components → Repair job approval.
